chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Drum and bass interplay with Clinton Walker and John Kirby
summary: With Walker he used hand signals to hold tempo; Kirby tended to pull the tempo back.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, that leads me to the next question that I had. And that is, up to this time, when you were playing with various bass players, I'd like to know just how you interacted with them. Well, both of you were keeping time. And sometimes, of course, one may go a little faster than the other, but the drummer is the important person in being able to keep the tempo where it's supposed to be. When you were with King Oliver and when he was recording with people like, say, Clinton Walker, who was his... He played tuba a lot. But how did you interact with Clinton Walker as a bass and drum combination there?
Well, we got along all right. Before we went in the studio, we would talk, just the two of us, you know, about getting things... He was able to get that good beat
Moore (III) - 51

and hold it right there. And I would go (?) right there with him. We would work together, don't get excited, don't get fast -- just one tempo. And we'd watch each other. So if we found ourselves getting a bit fast, he used to look at me, put up one hand to say it's all right, you know.
I see. So he gave you a lot of hand signals. And he would be playing the tuba at that time.
Yes.
Did Clinton Walker ever play the string bass, the bass fiddle?
Yes, he did.
He played both the bass fiddle and...
Yes. But King Oliver wanted him on bass.
Uh-huh, and not the tuba so much.
Well, the tuba...yeah, tuba, bass... You mean string bass.
String bass, yes.
Yeah, he had a string bass, but he didn't play it very much. Mostly he specialized in playing a tuba, which is the horn, the bass horn. He'd get a big sound.
Now, how about you and John Kirby as a combination? How did you fare? How did you do with Kirby?
Oh, I did all right with Kirby. Kirby had a tendency to pull the tempo back, you know.
Moore (III) - 52
Oh, is that right?
Yeah, he had a tendency to pull the tempo back.
That was something that he preferred to do, or was it just a tendency, do you think, on his part?
Well, not so much a tendency to me. Just the way he had felt, you know. I don't know whether he started getting tired in his fingers or what it was.
He wasn't playing behind the beat so much. It's just that the tempo would be pulled.
Yeah, the tempo would be going up and down.
Okay. And Pops Foster, of course, you got along all right with him as a combination.
Yes.
